summary: The Get started section of Business Central documentation covers orientation for newcomers and partners: product learning material, app development, selling and onboarding, FAQs, and help and support. It helps an agent route questions about what the product does, how partners build and sell, and where to find short answers.
overview:
Get started is the orientation section of the Business Central documentation. It has no pages of its own and is split into five subtopics: Learn, Develop, Sell, Frequently asked questions, and Help and support.

Learn suits newcomers. It gives a business functionality overview, application design details, process walkthroughs, Contoso Coffee demo data for practicing tasks, and partner resources and communities. Develop is for partners who build, customize, publish and maintain apps and extensions. Sell covers reselling online, onboarding customers and commercializing apps through Marketplace.

The FAQ subtopic gives short practical answers on AL development, marketplace validation, library and dependency apps, migration to Business Central online and the discontinued Windows client. Help and support has 10 pages, but this narrative doesn't describe what they cover.
key_points: Learn (6 pages) gives a product overview, application design details, process walkthroughs, Contoso Coffee demo data and partner resources and communities.
Develop (36 pages) is the largest subtopic. It covers getting started as a partner, per-tenant customization, localization, marketplace submission and validation, embed apps and app lifecycle.
Develop also explains Microsoft versus partner responsibilities in the online service.
Sell (5 pages) covers reselling online, onboarding customers, preparing company configuration packages, customizing the application and selling apps through Marketplace.
Sell also addresses partner setup, licensing and onboarding tools.
FAQ (9 pages) covers AL development, app testing, submission, updating and marketing validation for the marketplace.
FAQ also covers library and dependency apps, migration to Business Central online and the discontinued Windows client.
Help and support has 10 pages. This narrative doesn't describe what they cover.

issues: The overview and the last key point talk about the writing process ('no summary of its 10 pages was provided', 'not summarized in the input'). That doesn't help an agent. They now say Help and support has 10 pages and that its content isn't described here.
'Get started is the entry point to Business Central content' goes beyond the inputs. The inputs only show it as the Get started TOC section. The wording is softened.

The reading order ('Newcomers should start with Learn... Partners then move on to Develop') is the writer's own advice, not something in the summaries. It is now framed as a match between each subtopic and its audience.
Every other claim about Learn, Develop, Sell and FAQ, including the page counts, matches the subtopic summaries.
